analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate KIC from elastic modulus, Vickers hardness, indentation load and average crack length: KIC = 0.016 (E/HV)^(1/2) · P/c^(2/3)
analytical_models.model_note: c = 0.25·Σ(i=1..4) li, where li is the radial crack length from the indentation corners (Fig. 1).

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: FCC twins were frequently observed within the fine FCC Cu-rich particles located at β-Mn interfaces (SAED [011] beam pattern annotated 'FCC twin').
Fine FCC Cu-rich particles are evenly distributed at the interfaces between the β-Mn grains.

interfaces.interface_notes: Fig. 11 (b) SAED shows the fine interface particles are FCC (Cu-rich, depleted in Fe and Mn, slightly poor in Al) with FCC twins; β-Mn is poor in Cu according to EDS mapping.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (general sequence for Fe-Mn-Al-Cu steels); for this sample the α matrix had fully transformed to β-Mn after 600 °C/6 h aging.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Homogenized ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching. This is the parent state (proc_st-1100c-10min-oq) for the aging treatment.

Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h followed by water quenching. This sample corresponds to 600 °C for 6 h — the hardest condition of the 15Al alloy (965.6 HV).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness with load 9.8 N for 15 s, average of 5 measurements; fracture toughness by indentation technique with indentation load 9.8 N.
Agilent G200 Nanoindenter; indentation depth 200 nm; each test point spaced 5 μm or more apart; areas where indents did not contact FCC Cu-rich and BCC phases used for β-Mn intrinsic hardness.

phases_present.morphology: fine particles, elongated/lens-shaped, distributed at β-Mn interfaces

precipitates.distribution: evenly distributed at the interfaces between the β-Mn

structures.overall_structure: In the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h the α matrix completely disappeared and abundant near-equiaxed β-Mn formed; some fine particles are evenly distributed at the interfaces between the β-Mn. The fine particles exhibit an FCC crystalline structure (FCC Cu-rich phase) with FCC twins frequently observed within the particles; β-Mn is poor in Cu. EBSD also revealed a new BCC phase within the β-Mn in the ultra-hard alloys.

unmapped_findings: Ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g was achieved in the Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu (15Al) low-density steel (b0008, b0077); this corresponds to the hardest 15Al condition (965.6 HV at 600 °C/6 h) combined with its density of 6.85 g/cm³.

The β-Mn phase in the hardest 15Al sample (600 °C/6 h) contains Al 14.3 at.%, Mn 36.8 at.% and Cu 2.8 at.% (SEM-EDS, Fig. 14), and its Al content is lower than that of the 17Al and 19Al β-Mn, indicating Al increases the intrinsic β-Mn hardness only slightly by solid-solution strengthening (b0060, figure_014).

The 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h is the peak-hardness condition (965.6 HV) and the TEM sample chosen together with the 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h (924.9 HV) for microstructural analysis (b0055).
The phase evolution sequence for Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels during aging is: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (b0068).

For the 15Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range to achieve ultra-high hardness was mainly 525 °C–600 °C (b0038), and the hardness increased with increasing time up to ~6 h before slightly decreasing (b0037).
